title: Value objects
description:
Write classes that behave correctly in sets and maps.

```
new Point(1, 2).equals(new Point(1, 2)): true
set of 3 points with one duplicate: 2
map lookup with an equal key: found
mutable key changed: lookup fails (that is why keys must not change)
```
hints: `equals` checks `this == o`, then `o instanceof Point p && x == p.x && y == p.y`; `hashCode` returns `Objects.hash(x, y)` (lesson 7.02).
For the last part, write a small `MutableKey` class with a setter and the same `equals` and `hashCode`.
requirements: A `final class Point` (not a record) with `equals` and `hashCode` written by hand, consistent with each other.
Show a `HashSet<Point>` removing a duplicate and a `HashMap<Point, String>` lookup with an equal key.
Show what goes wrong when a key's fields change after it is put in a map.
stretch: Compare your `Point` with a `record Point2(int x, int y)`: the record writes all three methods for you.
